title: Fall Sales Put Inventory Planning in Focus for Ecommerce Sellers
summary: Amazon, Target, and Walmart launch fall sales as ecommerce sellers balance inventory, promotions, and profit margins ahead of the peak season.
body_markdown:
Amazon, Target, and Walmart are holding overlapping October sales, giving ecommerce sellers an opportunity to assess demand before the holiday season. According to a *Modern Retail*[article](https://www.modernretail.co/marketing/big-box-briefing-what-to-watch-for-as-amazon-target-and-walmart-host-their-fall-sales/) , Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days and Target’s Circle sale are scheduled for October 6–7, 2026. Walmart’s Fall Deals Sale runs October 5–11.


The events arrive as shoppers weigh seasonal purchases against everyday needs. *Modern Retail* ’s report adds that some consumers used summer Prime Day to stock up on essentials, while brands saw sales activity spread across competing channels.


For ecommerce sellers, the overlap puts attention on inventory allocation and profitability. Participating across marketplaces means balancing available stock with promotional prices, while accounting for freight and other costs that affect margins.


Sellers can review each product’s margin before choosing discounts, allocate inventory by channel, and monitor sales throughout each event. Use those results to revisit replenishment plans for later holiday promotions. Reviewing order volumes alongside fulfillment capacity can also help you assess whether delivery commitments remain realistic.


October results provide one reference point for planning; they do not establish how customers will spend across the holiday season.
